text.p: Leucadia National Corp's life and property-casualty insurance companies are known for the direct marketing of their insurance products and are likely to attract interest from buyers seeking new distribution methods, industry sources said.
Leucadia National on Wednesday said several companies have expressed interest in the acquisition of certain of its insurance operations and said it was in talks with certain interested parties.
The company said the price ranges being discussed for such insurance operations are substantially in excess of the book value of these operations.
The combined statutory capital of Leucadia's three main life insurance operations is about $400 million, A.M. Best senior vice president Larry Mayewski said.
And a buyer might pay a multiple of about 1.25 to 1.5 times the statutory capital for those properties, he said.
Leucadia rose one, or nearly four percent, to 28-3/4.
Leucadia declined to say which of its insurance operations may be up for sale and declined any additional comment.
The New York-based diversified financial services company, owns four life and two property-casualty insurance operations.
And it's the distribution through direct marketing techniques, such as television and telephone marketing that distinguishes the company and makes it an attractive target, industry sources said.
The acquisition of Leucadia's businesses would be a move to expand distribution sources rather than to consolidate through cost cutting, an industry source said.
Any of the large, life insurance acquirors might be interested in such a property, he said.
Potential acquisitors could include American General Corp, General Electric Co's GE Capital and Conseco Inc.
American General declined comment. Conseco and GE Capital were not immediately available for comment.
Leucadia's life insurance businesses consist of Colonial Penn Life, Charter National Life, Intramerica and Providential Life.
Its property-casualty companies consist of Colonial Penn Property & Casualty and Empire Group, according to recent filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Colonial Penn Life sells graded benefit life insurance to primarily the 50-and-over age group and Charter National Life provides variable annuities, said A.M. Best assistant vice president Tom Upton.
Intramerica sells both of those products in New York state and Providential Life is a recent, small acquisition.
Leucadia's Colonial Penn Property & Casualty and Empire Group provide personal and commercial property-casualty insurance.
